cases.title: Vertical plate 0.6 m, Ts 90 C, ambient 30 C (Churchill and Chu)
cases.reference: Lecture-note Example 9.1 (Al-Mustaqbal Univ. College, Heat Transfer, natural convection; Cengel-style, air at 60 C: k 0.02808, nu 1.896e-5, Pr 0.722): published Ra 7.656e8, Nu 113.4. The source's own Ra arithmetic is 0.15 % below an independent recompute (7.668e8), so Ra gets 0.5 %.

cases.title: Horizontal plate 0.6 x 0.6 m, Ts 90 C, ambient 30 C
cases.reference: Cengel, Heat Transfer: A Practical Approach 2nd ed., Example 9-2 (also reproduced in lecture notes): Lc = A/p = 0.15 m, air at 60 C. Published Ra 1.196e7 and hot-face-down Nu = 0.27 Ra^(1/4) = 15.86. (The book also applies 0.54 Ra^(1/4) = 31.76 to the hot-face-up case at Ra above 1e7; Forge uses the 0.15 Ra^(1/3) branch there, as Incropera does, so that number is not tested.)

cases.title: Horizontal plate, hot face up and down at Ra = 222 593
cases.reference: SFU ENSC 388 (Bahrami) solution-manual line as printed: Ra = 222 593 gives Nu = 11.73 (0.54 Ra^(1/4), hot face up) and 5.865 (0.27 Ra^(1/4), hot face down). Only the printed Ra and Nu pair is used; the problem's other inputs were not checked.

cases.title: Radiation from the sealed box of Cengel Example 15-10
cases.reference: Cengel, Heat and Mass Transfer 3rd ed., Example 15-10 (McGraw-Hill free chapter 15): eps 0.85, area 0.21 + 0.12 m2, Ts 65 C = 338 K, room 35 C = 308 K: published Q_rad = 64.5 W. h_r (Ts^2+Ta^2)(Ts+Ta) eps sigma equals eps sigma (Ts^4 - Ta^4)/(Ts - Ta) exactly.

cases.title: Air properties at 60 C, 1 atm
cases.reference: Table A-15 values quoted in Cengel Examples 9-2 and 15-10 (via the sources above): k = 0.02808 W/m K, nu = 1.896e-5 m2/s, Pr = 0.7202 at 333 K. The property fits claim about 3 %: the Incropera and Cengel tables themselves differ by about 2 %.

cases.title: Stack flow through two 1000 mm2 openings 0.1 m apart
cases.reference: Derived by hand from V = Cd A_eff sqrt(2 g H (Ti - To) / Ti), A_eff = A1 A2 / sqrt(A1^2 + A2^2), Cd 0.6, Ti 330 K, To 300 K, computed separately in Python: 1.79149e-4 m3/s.

cases.title: Two-resistor chain with a heat source
Outer surface of the sealed box of Cengel Example 15-10 held at 65 C, room 35 C
cases.reference: Cengel, Heat and Mass Transfer 3rd ed., Example 15-10 (McGraw-Hill free chapter 15): box 0.40 x 0.30 x 0.15 m, eps 0.85, bottom insulated (on a stand), Ts 65 C, room 35 C: published convection 48.2 W (sides 33.6 + top 14.6), radiation 64.5 W, total 112.7 W. Radiation is exact. Convection differs by construction: the book uses a simplified correlation with Lc = 4A/p for the top face, Forge uses Churchill-Chu and A/P (Incropera), which gives a higher top-face coefficient; natural-convection correlations are good to about 15 %, so convection gets 15 % and the total 8 %. The bottom face is insulated with a zero-conductance contact. Split by face (reported, not asserted): the four sides give 32.6 W against the book's 33.6 W (3 %), the top gives 21.1 W against 14.6 W (45 % high), so the aggregate band hides a large top-face difference that comes from the book's simplified top-face correlation and length.

customMaterials.name: Painted metal (eps 0.85)
customMaterials.notes: Test material: thin metal wall with a painted outer surface, as in the textbook case.

cases.title: 60 x 40 x 25 mm ABS box with a board and one 1 W component
cases.reference: Conservation of energy (exact): at steady state the heat leaving through the outer surface and vents equals the 1 W dissipated, so the balance error is zero to solver precision; total_heat echoes the input. Not a comparison with a measurement.
